content: Hedeoma pulegioides, commonly known as American Pennyroyal or American False Pennyroyal, is a species of the Hedeoma genus that is native to eastern North America. Its range extends from Nova Scotia and southern Ontario westward to Minnesota and South Dakota, and southward to northern Georgia and Arkansas. This plant is a low-growing, strongly aromatic, herbaceous annual that typically reaches a height of 15 to 30 cm. It features a slender, erect, and highly branched stem that is somewhat hairy and square in shape. The leaves are small, thin, and relatively narrow, emitting a strong mint-like odor and possessing a pungent taste. The flowers of Hedeoma pulegioides are pale blue, hermaphroditic, and grow in small clusters. The plant blooms from mid to late summer. It is also known by several other names, including mock pennyroyal, squaw mint, tickweed, stinking balm, mosquito plant, and American false pennyroyal. The species name pulegioides is derived from the Latin words pulegium and oides, which together mean like pennyroyal. Hedeoma pulegioides is also recognized by its synonyms, including Melissa pulegioides L. (its basionym), Cunila pulegioides (L.), and Ziziphora pulegioides (L.) Desf. The term Pennyroyal (or Pennyrile, a dialectal variation) is also used to describe a geographic region in western Kentucky, known as the Pennyroyal Plateau. This area was named after the plant, which once grew there in such abundance that it lent its name to the entire region.
